sections.title: The moat, card by card

items.title: l'Art
items.body:
Floating a stable stable soundfield in a room devoid of any sweet spot is what the entire industry has missed.

Stereo is *already* 3D when implemented properly.

The l'Art stack does not enhance stereo by addition — It does the opposite: generates a more realistic stereo performance while completely eliminating stereo's only real downside: the sweet spot.
list: Part of patent moat on Acoustic teleportation codec
Sweet-spot elimination (wave-field synthesis lineage)
Broadcast-optimized capture pipeline
Artist-owned stereo · AGF-owned l'Art · 50/50 broadcast mixed
5-layer active filtering pipeline (proven on the Core)
Apple bought 1,000pc Relay runs at full wholesale multiple times — reason unknown / unconfirmed (the units never sold through)
A Fraunhofer research scientist was the only outside party who ever grokked the broader concept; sold a rudimentary version to Sennheiser
kv: The Core's wave-field synthesis tuning appealed to premium-to-high-end dealers globally — not because it threw sound around, but because it presented a stable stereo soundfield indistinguishable from a pair of premium bookshelves + sub.
items.note: Patent status differs between document versions: Patented (July 6) versus Trade secret (July 14). Shown as the newer one. This must be settled before publication.

items.eyebrow: stereOS — Global OS for Performing Arts
items.title: stereOS
items.pull: The global operating system for performing arts.
items.body: Third parties don't license codecs. They adopt AGF's application-specific implementation of stereOS. Kernel and key IP enclaves locked. Application-space open without restriction. Bootlegs inevitable, social faux-pas, addressable. The walled garden, the way Steve Jobs learned to build one: safe, stable, requirements not daunting, content positioned as premium.
list: Locked kernel + locked IP enclaves
Open application space (no restriction)
Walled-garden content positioning (Jobs-style)
Acquisition / hostile-service / integration — the only three options for ten-ton gorillas
Bootlegs are inevitable but positioned as a **social faux-pas**
not a piracy panic — community membership is the deterrent
Device-level lockout: capturing patented content for illicit distribution permanently bans the user from the AGF hardware ecosystem
Legal remedies pursued by AGF on behalf of the artist to recover proceeds from illicit marketing
kv: The lessons from Sony's L-Cassette, DSD, MiniDisc, DAT, digital watermarking — all attempts to lock down media in service of global domination, all failed. AGF takes the iOS-after-macOS lesson instead.

items.title: BT'N-Tech
items.body: A class of technologies, liberally applied. From analog-based toroidal chokes to multi-stage waveform regeneration. The flagship is comprehensive home/facility power regeneration — well known at the industrial scale (Schneider), virtually absent in consumer/commercial audio. R&D on the high-power regeneration strategy is non-trivial but well-scoped; the hidden benefit propagates throughout every product and the entire strategy.
list: Modular finished product line (passive smoothing → full regeneration)
Native in-circuit smoothing on every AGF component
Algorithmic noise shaping where target semis demand
Comprehensive home/facility power regeneration (flagship)
**Well-known at industrial scale (Schneider Electric); virtually absent in consumer audio** — the entire seam
kv:
Schneider does this at industrial scale; nobody owns the position for Consumer -> Pro at scale.

Every extra dB of S/N ratio compounds across the entire system making the other acoustic technologies more powerful.

items.title: l'espacI/O
items.body: Combines observed importance of music recording with virtual acoustic scene creation. Maps the acoustic space from a performance-capture perspective (pro line), then impresses the character of that space on the consumer side — the initial sensory experience of 'being transported,' then persistent reinforcement of the illusion. The illusion is compressed by the algorithm; compute overhead is minimized; every extra dB of spatial capture is fought for via BT'N-Tech.
list: Performance-capture spatial mapping (pro line)
Consumer-side spatial impression + reinforcement
Algorithmic compression of the illusion
Compounds with BT'N-Tech S/N gains
**Maps the acoustic space first** — from a performance-capture perspective on the pro line — **then impresses that character** onto the consumer device
**Two-phase sensory loop**: initial transport experience ("being there") + persistent sensory reinforcement that keeps the illusion stable across long-form listening
kv: Owning the signal path from Capture -> In-Home render is what unlocks a convincing Acoustic Teleportation: *That's affordable to implement*

items.eyebrow: FRC41 — Front Row Center For One
items.title: FRC41
items.body: Abstractly related to HRTF optimization — commercially attempted many times, always failed through overthinking. The solution takes a page from Amar Bose's greatest strength: Understanding the fine art of good enough. Tiny processing expense, near-zero latency penalty. The psycho-acoustic sound-field generated *inside your head* instantly morphs into a 3D sound experience.
list: Minimal processing footprint
Near-zero latency penalty
Psycho-acoustic sound-field externalization
Cascading benefit from prior AGF technologies
kv: Prior attempts have over-thought the implementation. The fine art of good enough wins commercially every time.

items.title: No-Nails
items.pull: To a hammer, every problem looks like a nail; No engineering domain-hammers allowed.
items.body:
Conceptualized to eliminate brute-forcing problems. No layer of the product is taken for granted. The "Mercy Catch-All" = The amount of details that in combination could likely be patented is vast. One of the speaker designs produces a visceral bass output reaching below 30Hz via transmission-line, audibly balanced at low volumes. This is unheard of in anything but cost-no-object designs, these will cost a couple hundred bucks to build in low-hundreds volume.

Each engineering layer enhances modestly. No one element carries the load. No over-processed sound. No sucked-out life. The sum of the design in a league of its own.

When this process is applied diligently, application specific patents are unavoidable; we'll be tripping over them during every development.
list: Mechanical: transmission-line tuning over inert-cabinet brute force
Materials: combinations of acoustic materials relieved purely digital interventions
Analog Electronics: transformer arrays and ultra-low-noise resistors + polypropylene caps eliminated or shaped noise
Multi-Stage DSP: Allow complex filters without flagship parts
kv: Every discipline contributes meaningfully. No one element overloaded. The result sounds delightfully natural. When the hammer is applied, you're guaranteed a bland life-less sound.

sections.note: Capabilities and advantages are the July 14 version. The July 6 version (content/sections/technology.v2.json) adds a few lines worth considering: Sony America's California R&D had similar tech and 'the marketing guys completely ruined it'; No-Nails lists beryllium-alloy HF in the dustcap position and light final-stage DSP; FRC41's effect is described as moving to a pair of high-end speakers in the sweet spot.
